title: Amputation and ostomy status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM status codes this note supports.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for gastrointestinal health and stoma history.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old male presenting today for a routine follow-up regarding his history of bowel surgery. He reports that he previously had an ileostomy. He underwent a surgical reversal of the stoma several years ago and is currently living without a stoma. He reports that his digestion has been stable since the takedown procedure. He denies any current abdominal pain, persistent diarrhea, or significant changes in bowel habits. He states he feels well and has no concerns regarding his nutritional intake or energy levels.

Review of Systems
Negative for fever, chills, weight loss, or abdominal pain. Denies nausea, vomiting, or shortness of breath. Denies any changes in appetite.

Social History
The patient is retired and lives at home with his wife. He enjoys walking and gardening. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Father had hypertension. Mother had a history of stroke.

Medication List
Multivitamin daily.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 128/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Height: 5'10"
Weight: 185 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 210 x 10^9/L
Glucose: 105 mg/dL
eGFR: 82 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
General: The patient is alert and oriented x3. He appears well-nourished and in no acute distress.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants. No masses or guarding noted.
Skin: Intact, no signs of irritation or breakdown.

Assessment
1. Status post ileostomy reversal. The patient is clinically stable and asymptomatic following the surgical reversal of his previous stoma.

Plan
1. Continue current activity level.
2. Follow up in 6 months for routine monitoring.
3. Encouraged to maintain a high-fiber diet to support healthy digestion following the takedown.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: The ileostomy was reversed: the patient no longer has one, so there is no status to report.

distractors.why: A reversed ileostomy is no longer present.
